turns.text: I keep thinking about work long after I close my laptop. By dinner I feel flat, and I am still waiting for another message to come in.
What tends to happen between finishing work and sitting down for dinner?
I usually check my phone. If there is a late message, I read it straight away and start planning a reply, even if it can wait until morning.
You mentioned one evening that felt a little different. What do you remember about it?
On Tuesday I put on some music while making dinner. I did not suddenly feel great, but I was less caught up in work for a while.
It sounds as though having something of your own in the evening mattered to you. What else might feel enjoyable or meaningful?
I could call my sister on Saturday. We have not spoken properly in a while, and I usually enjoy talking with her.
I could also draw for ten minutes after work. I used to do that a lot, but I have not picked up my sketchbook recently.
Listening to a whole album one evening sounds nice too. Or I might take a short walk at lunchtime if the weather is good.
Of those ideas, is there one you want to commit to now?
Not a particular one. Calling my sister would feel meaningful, drawing would be fun, and a walk might be easier on a busy day. I would rather decide when I see how the week goes.
We could set aside ten minutes on Tuesday, or leave it for the weekend. How would you like to approach it?
Those are possibilities, but I do not want to promise Tuesday, the weekend, or a set number of minutes.
Would you be willing to make time for one enjoyable or meaningful activity this week, with the choice left open?
Yes. I will make time for one thing I enjoy or find meaningful this week. I will choose what it is when I am ready, rather than trying to do all four ideas.
So we have not agreed that you specifically need to call, draw, listen to music, or walk?
Right. Those are ideas, not four separate tasks. I am agreeing to one activity of my choice.
What might make that difficult?
Late work messages can swallow the evening. Thursday is also busy because I pick up my niece, so I do not want this to become another rigid appointment.
We can keep that flexibility in mind. Would it be useful to record your mood as well, to notice how your days feel?
Yes, I will record my mood each evening around eight, thinking about the whole day rather than just the last hour.
How would you like to rate it?
I can use zero to ten, with zero as my worst day and ten as my best day.
You also mentioned noticing your energy. Do you want that in the check-in?
I can add an energy rating if I feel like it, but mood is the part I definitely want to record.
A short journal might be another option to talk about later. Do you want to start that now?
No, not now. Maybe we can talk about it at another session.
What would you like us to look at next time?
I would like to notice whether the evenings feel any different when I give myself a little space after work. We can look at that together next time.
Yes, we can compare what you noticed then.
